lawyer:
Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellants
Md. Ataul Huq, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondents.
parties:
Sudhir Kumar Das and another ----- Appellants
Vs.
Abdul Malek Mia and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated March 29, 2001 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 315 of 1981).
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: The appeal, by leave, is against the judgment dated March 29, 2001 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 315 of 1981 allowing the same upon setting aside the judgment and order dated September 23, 1980 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Barisal in Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 1979 dismissing the same. The Miscellaneous Case was registered upon an application filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The same was filed seeking getting aside of the ex parte decree dated December 19, 1978 passed in Title Suit No. 77 of 1965.

2. The appellants filed Title Suit No. 77 of 1965 seeking setting aside of the decree dated September 26, 1962 passed in Title Suit No. 468 of 1962.

3. The respondent No.1 was the defendant No. 2 in Title Suit No. 77 of 1965. He upon service of summons entered appearance and filed written statement. While the suit was awaiting for disposal before the trial Court, as seen from the materials on record in connection with the civil revision the record of the Title Suit No. 77 of 1965 was called for by the High Court Division and after disposal of the civil revision the records were sent down. After receiving the records by the trial Court fresh summons was issued to the defendants and after receiving the service return date was fixed for taking steps and the order so passed by the Court was shown to the defendant's (herein respondent No. 1) Advocate on May 26, 1978. The suit was fixed for peremptory hearing on December 19, 1978 and on that date the suit was decreed ex parte. The respondent No.1 who was defendant No.2 in the suit filed application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on April 19, 1979 seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree dated December 19, 1978 alleging that he was not aware of the receiving of the record from the High Court Division by the trial Court and that summons was not served on him after receiving back of the record from the High Court Division and that his Advocate engaged prior to calling for the records by the High Court Division in connection with civil revision did not inform him about the receiving of the record from the High Court Division by the trial Court and that also about the date for taking steps after receiving of the record from the High Court Division and finally about the date of peremptory hearing of the suit and, as such, he was not aware of the ex parte decree and that for the first time he came to know about the ex parte decree from Shamsher Ali Sheikh (PW 2) on 2nd of Baishakh, 1386 BS.

4. The Miscellaneous case was opposed by filing written objection stating, inter alia, that after receiving the record from the High Court Division the date was communicated to the petitioner through his learned Advocate and that summons was duly served on the petitioner and the petitioner was fully aware of the date of peremptory hearing of the suit and intentionally allowed the suit to be disposed of ex parte with the object of harassing the plaintiff-opposite party. It was also contended that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation and, as such, liable to be dismissed.

5. The petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case, i.e. respondent No.1 herein, in support of his case of initial knowledge about the ex parte decree examined himself as PW 1 and his cultivator, PW 2 and also examined another witness in support of his contention that summons was not served on him. The opposite party in the Miscellaneous Case examined the process server and the person in whose presence the summons was served as well as himself.

6. The trial Court, on the findings that petitioner i.e. respondent No.1, failed to adduce any tangible evidence either oral or documentary to substantiate his case of knowing about the ex parte decree for the first time on 2nd of Baishakh, 1386 BS., that the petitioner to substantiate his contention that his learned Advocate did not inform him the date of peremptory hearing of the suit, has not examined his Advocate, that although petitioner in his deposition stated that he came to know about the arrival of the record from the High Court Division on April 26, 1976 but he has not stated how he came to know about the arrival of the record and, as such, his said contention cannot be accepted, that his contention that he did not know anything about the suit after receiving of the record from the High Court Division and consequent thereupon the suit was decreed ex parte has not been established, that summons was served on the petitioner, i.e. respondent No.1, on May 8, 1978, that in the background of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record it can be said that the petitioner was aware of the position of the suit after arrival of the record from the High Court Division, that the petitioner failed to prove his contention that he for the first time came to know about the ex parte decree on 2nd of Baishakh, 1386 BS dismissed the Miscellaneous case on the ground of limitation. The trial Court also held "that there was no sufficient cause for non appearance of the petitioner when the suit was called on for hearing". As against the judgment of the trial Court the respondent No.1 filed First Miscellaneous Appeal before the High Court Division.

7. The High Court Division, in the background of the contention of the appellant that his learned Advocate did not inform him about the receiving of the record by the trial Court from the High Court Division and also about the date of peremptory hearing of the suit, observed that the suit was decreed ex parte due to fault or laches of the Advocate of the appellant and, as such, he should not suffer for the laches and negligence of his Advocate. The High Court Division also observed that as the summons was served by hanging on the fencing of the 'ghor' (sic) and, as such, "it is unsafe to infer that defendant No.2 had knowledge about the date of hearing of the Title Suit No.77 of 1965" and that "Learned court below was not legally justified in holding that the said service vide Exhibit A was a good service according to law and that defendant No. 2 had knowledge about the date of the said suit. The High Court Division was of the view that even if the engaged lawyer was informed vide order No. 47 dated 2-5-78 that will be the knowledge of the lawyer not of the party unless sufficiently proved by facts and circumstances, that if due to laches or fault of the lawyer the suit was decreed ex parte, the party (defendant No. 2) should not be made liable for that", that from the evidence of the witness examined by the opposite party (in the Miscellaneous Case) and upon perusal of the Exhibit A (service return) it is seen that the service of summons "was not personal but the substituted service by hanging on the fencing of the ghor (sic)", that the witness No. 1 and witness No. 2 of the opposite party (in the Miscellaneous Case) are not uniform on vital point and, as such, on the basis of their evidence it cannot be said that the summons was duly served on the petitioner (in the Miscellaneous Case). The High Court Division finally held "that there were sufficient causes for defendant No.2 (appellant) A. Malek Meah preventing him from attending the court on the date fixed for hearing and due to default of any step by him Title Suit No. 77 of 1965 was decreed ex parte setting aside the decree dated 26-9-62 of Title Suit No. 468 of 1962 which the defendant No.2 had interest to protect and for which he filed written statement in Title Suit No.77 of 1965 long ago to contest, if the ex parte decree of Title Suit No. 77 of 1965 stands due to dismissal of Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 1979 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure vide impugned judgment the appellant (defendant No. 2) A. Malek will be seriously prejudiced sustaining loss and will be deprived finally of the chance to contest for disposal of the suit on merit". On the aforesaid findings and observations the High Court Division upon allowing the appeal set aside the judgment of the trial Court.

8. Leave was obtained for consideration of the contention that ex parte decree was passes: on December 19, 1978 and the Miscellaneous case was filed on April 19, 1979 alleging date of knowledge on 2nd of Baishakh, 1386 BS which was not proved and consequent thereupon the Court of first instance having had held that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation and that the said finding having not been reversed by the High Court Division and thereby finding of the Court of first instance as to limitation as remains unreversed, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law and that without reversing the finding of fact as to service of summons the High Court Division having had come to a wrong finding that the defendant No. 2 was prevented by sufficient cause, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law.

9. Point for consideration in the appeal whether after receiving the record from the High Court Division summons issued to the respondent No. 1, i.e. defendant No. 2, was served on him and the service of summons in the manner was a good service and the contention of the respondent No.1 that his engaged Advocate did not inform him about the arrival of the record as well as about the date of peremptory hearing of the suit in spite of informing the learned Advocate about arrival of record was established by the respondent No. 2 and whether the respondent No.1 i.e. defendant No. 2, the petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case established the date of his initial knowledge about the ex parte decree dated December 19, 1978. It may be mentioned the Miscellaneous case was filed on April 19, 1979 stating that the respondent No.1 came to know about the ex parte decree on 2nd of Baishakh, 1386 BS from PW 2 who was told about the ex parte decree by certain Kala Sarker.

10. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence of PW 1 i.e. petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case and the PW 2, held that plaintiff miserably failed to establish that he for the first time came to know about the ex parte decree on 2nd of Baishakh, 1386 BS. The trial Court discarded the evidence of PW 2 not being a disinterested witness since PW 1 stated that PW 2 is his cultivator. The trial Court also noticed in the evidence of PW 2 that Kala Sarker was present in Court while PW 2 was deposing but said Kala Sarker was not examined without offering any explanation from the side of the petitioner in the Miscellaneous case. The trial Court in the background of the evidence on record held that the petitioner i.e. respondent No.1 herein, did not establish the date of initial knowledge by tangible evidence. The trial Court rejected the contention of the respondent No.1 that his learned Advocate did not inform him about the arrival of the record from the High Court Division as well as about the date of peremptory hearing of the suit since the learned Advocate was not examined and no explanation was offered for not examining him.

<u>11. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view that respondent No.1 having not been corroborated as to his contention that his learned Advocate did not inform him about the arrival of the record at the trial Court from the High Court Division and the date of peremptory hearing, the trial Court rightly rejected the said contention. The High Court Division was of the view that knowledge of the Advocate of the respondent No. 1 as to arrival of record at the trial Court from High Court Division as well as about the date of peremptory hearing was not in the knowledge of the respondent No.1 and that for the aches of the Advocate of the respondent No.1 he should not suffer. We like to observe that High Court Division was quite unmindful of the fact that the contention of the respondent No.1 of not having any information from his engaged Advocate about the receiving of the record by the trial Court and of fixation of the suit for peremptory hearing was not established by any reliable evidence. Now the question is, whether summons was served on the respondent No.1 who was petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case. The respondent No.1 as PW 1 deposed that summons was not served on him and he tried to establish that fact by the evidence of PW 3 who deposed that in his presence no summons was served on the respondent No.1. It may be mentioned on scrutiny of the service return the trial Court noticed that name of PW 3 did not appear in the service return as Mokabela witness and, as such, the trial Court discarded his evidence. It may also be mentioned that this PW has stated that he did not receive any summons from Court for deposing in the case. PW 1 has also not said that he took out summons in the name of the PW 3. In that state of the matter, it appears that the said witness was procured to depose something about which he had no idea. The trial Court, on consideration of the evidence of OPW 3, the process server and OPW 1 person whose name appeared in the service return as Mokabela witness and also on consideration of the evidence of OPW 2 who was opposite party No. 4 in the Miscellaneous Case, held that summons was duly served on the respondent No.1 i.e. the petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case. Since the Miscellaneous case was filed beyond the period of limitation and that as the petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case failed to establish his initial date of knowledge about the ea- parte decree, the trial Court dismissed the Miscellaneous Case on the finding of limitation. The respondent No.1 tried to establish the date of knowledge of the ex parte decree by the evidence of PW 2, who being cultivator of the respondent No.1 trial Court considered him not disinterested witness, in our view, quite legally, but High Court Division without reversing the finding of the trial Court on limitation set aside the judgment of the trial Court.</u>

<u>12. The High Court Division set aside the judgment and order of the trial Court on the ground that the manner in which the summons was served, i.e. by hanging, being not personal service the same was not a good service since the service of summons "was a substitutory service by hanging on the fencing of the ghor and not personal service on defendant No. 2 A. Malek Meah" i.e. petitioner in the Miscellaneous case. It is in the evidence of OPW 1, whose name appeared in the service return, Exhibit A, that process server offered the summons to the petitioner in the Miscellaneous case i.e. respondent No.1 and he having had refused to accept the summons, process server served the summons by hanging on the fencing of the hut. Considering the evidence of OPW 1 along with the evidence of OPW 3 we are of the view service of summons on the respondent No.1, was quite good service and the High Court Division was in serious error in holding that the summons served in the manner was not a good service. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division discarded the evidence of OPW 1 and OPW 3 upon observing that they differed with each other on some vital points. The High Court Division while making the said observation did not specify on which vital point the said witnesses differed with each other. The High Court Division while disposing of the appeal did not discuss the evidence of the said witnesses. We are of the view that High Court Division was in error in discarding the evidence of OPW 1 and OPW 3 without discussing and considering the evidence of the said witnesses and specifying in what particular point they differed. The High Court Division was of the view that respondent No.1 should not suffer for the laches and negligence of his learned Advocate and thereupon was of the view that Miscellaneous Case was required to be allowed to give a chance to the respondent No.1 to contest the suit since relief sought in the suit was for setting aside a decree obtained by the respondent No.1 in an earlier suit. With due respect to the learned Judge of the High Court Division we like to mention that the learned Judge was quite unmindful of the fact whether the petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case established the laches and negligence of his learned Advocate in not informing about arrival of record from the High Court Division and also date of peremptory hearing or, in other words, whether the petitioner's contention that his engaged Advocate did not inform him about the receiving of the record from the High Court Division and fixing the case for peremptory hearing was at all established. From the judgment of the High Court Division it is not seen that the High Court Division arrived at any such finding that petitioner i.e. respondent No.1, established his contention that his engaged Advocate did not inform him about the arrival of the record from the High Court Division and the fixation of the case for peremptory hearing. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record held that petitioner, i.e. respondent No.1, failed to establish his contention that his engaged Advocate did not inform him about the receiving of the record by the trial Court and fixing the case for peremptory hearing. This vital finding of the trial Court was not reversed by the High Court Division. The High Court Division while setting aside the judgment of the trial Court also did not reverse the finding of the trial Court that the petitioner i.e. respondent No.1 failed to establish his initial date of knowledge about the ex parte decree. The High Court Division in setting aside the judgment of the trial Court did not advert itself to the question of limitation as considered by the trial Court. The first Court of appeal being the last Court of fact while reversing the judgment appealed is required to dispose of the appeal on independent discussion of the evidence relied upon by the Court of first instance and to assign reason for reversing or rejecting the finding and reasoning given by the trial Court while setting aside or reversing the judgment of the said Court. The appellate Court is also required to arrive at independent finding in support of its disagreement with the finding and decision of the trial Court or, in other words, while considering the finding and decision of the trial Court erroneous. In the instant case the High Court Division as the last Court of fact was required to discuss the evidence and to record reason for not placing reliance on the evidence which was considered reliable by the trial Court in making its decision, but the said established procedure was not complied with by the High Court Division while reversing the judgment and decision of the trial Court.</u>

13. In the background of the discussions made herein-above we find merit in the appeal.

14. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. There is no order as to costs.

End.
